title: The failed-held restart-resume fork case re-implements the resume loop in the test, picking the first dex of the pool type and passing ctx.chain.snipeAmount exactly as production does, so it pins the registered wrong-dex and wrong-probe-amount S1s as the expected restart behaviour

evidence.note: the test reads getResumeAntiRugTrades and, per row, does ctx.chain.dexes.find(d => d.dexType === r.pool_type), resumeExitMonitor(..., ctx.chain.snipeAmount, ...) and registerAntiRugPosition itself
production resumeMultiChainMonitoring: first dex of the type and ctx.chain.snipeAmount (AUD-EXIT-013, AUD-EXIT-015)
production anti-rug resume: first dex of the type (AUD-ANTIRUG-011)
the seeded position is on uniswap-v2 (the first V2 dex), so the first-dex choice is also right by coincidence
failed-held state is written with markExitFailedHeld / updateTradeStatus directly, not by a failed sell

sibling_sites_checked: Other resume drivers: botWiring (anti-rug resume with mocked SQL, AUD-TESTI-006), the unit restart-resume test (AUD-TESTU-005). Test 1 and Test 2 of this file resume with "0.05", the same as the buy amount.
severity_rationale: S2: the strongest real-path resume proof in the suite asserts the production SQL (sound) but copies the defective dex and amount choice into the test, hiding AUD-EXIT-013, AUD-EXIT-015 and AUD-ANTIRUG-011.
recommendation: Phase 28: call resumeMultiChainMonitoring and resumeAntiRugMonitoring themselves, seed the position on a second V2 dex (sushiswap-v2) with a buy amount different from snipeAmount, and assert the dex and probe amount the monitor and detector use (RED today).
affected_cases: a restart resumes an exit_failed_held row into monitoring + re-registers anti-rug
escaped_regression: Today: a failed-held position bought on sushiswap-v2 is resumed and re-registered on uniswap-v2 after a restart (AUD-EXIT-013 / AUD-ANTIRUG-011) and this case stays green because it performs the same lookup itself on a uniswap-v2 position.
